minor.issue: EXIF orientation is only normalised when the recompression path triggers (size>1MB OR mime=image/png OR long_edge>2048). A small JPEG (<1MB, <=2048px) with EXIF orientation set is stored AS-IS without applying ImageOps.exif_transpose. Mobile camera shots often carry orientation tags but may be under 1MB. Suggest: also set needs_recompress=True when EXIF tag 0x0112 is present and !=1.

rca of the issue: Only one finding: EXIF orientation is not applied when image bypasses the compression path. RCA: _compress_image_bytes (server.py:1083) computes `needs_recompress = len(content) > COMPRESS_THRESHOLD_BYTES or mime.lower() == 'image/png'`, and short-circuits with `return content, mime, w, h` when neither resize nor recompress is needed. The `im = ImageOps.exif_transpose(im)` call only runs when one of the conditions triggers. Fix: also flag `needs_recompress = True` when `im.getexif().get(0x0112, 1) != 1`, or unconditionally apply exif_transpose+re-save when EXIF orientation is non-trivial.
